title: Policy-driven role fabric with context-aware scope inheritance and audit hooks
creator: Sofia Chen
summary: Design a next-generation RBAC model (v2) that uses a policy-driven role fabric. The model must support fine-grained resource hierarchies, context-aware scope inheritance, explicit grant auditing, SSO/SAML group-to-role mapping, and admin controls (delegation, emergency breakglass, and approval workflows).
background: Current RBAC (v1) is coarse-grained: roles are tenant-scoped with limited inheritance and no first-class audit hooks. As customers adopt Dedicated and Private deployments, they need predictable, auditable authorization boundaries and flexible admin delegation. RBAC v2 should support cross-tenant admin roles for platform operators while ensuring tenant isolation and clear audit trails.
goals: 1) Define a role and permission primitive model that composes via policies. 2) Specify resource hierarchy and deterministic inheritance rules. 3) Produce a permissions matrix covering typical Redwood resources. 4) Design migration and compatibility layer for v1 customers. 5) Integrate audit logging metadata and SSO/SAML mapping patterns. 6) Provide admin controls (delegation, approval, emergency access) with guardrails.
non_goals: 1) Implementing the policy engine runtime (implementation tracked in ENG-91000). 2) Changes to billing permissions outside RBAC semantics. 3) Replacing existing SSO providers; we only define mapping patterns and hooks.
proposal: Introduce a policy-driven role fabric where 'RoleSets' are collections of 'RoleBindings' that attach to 'Principals' (users/groups/service accounts). Roles are defined as named policy templates referencing permission primitives. Scopes are explicit and hierarchical; role bindings evaluate with context (resource path, time, request attributes). The system enforces a deny-by-default base policy and supports explicit allow rules, exception rules, and conditional grants (e.g., time-limited, approval-required).
resource_hierarchy: Canonical resource types (ordered parent -> child): organization -> region -> account -> tenant -> project -> model -> deployment -> route -> invocation_token. Console objects (dashboards, alerts, rollouts) are namespaced under project. Each resource exposes a resource_identifier (urn-like) and ancestry array used in policy evaluation.
scope_semantics: Scope kinds: global, organization, account, tenant, project, resource. Inheritance rules: grants at a higher scope apply to all descendant resources unless explicitly shadowed by a deny at a lower scope. Conditional bindings can override inheritance when a condition evaluates true (e.g., 'in emergency_mode'). Bindings include metadata: creator, created_at, grant_reason, expiration, approval_reference, and delegated_by.
permission_primitives: read, list, write, create, delete, deploy, scale, manage_keys, manage_roles, grant_role, revoke_role, impersonate, view_audit, export_audit, billing_read, billing_write, configure_sso, manage_policy, approve_elevations.
roles_catalog_summary: Suggested role templates: viewer (read/list), developer (read, create, deploy on project+), operator (deploy, scale, observe), manager (full project lifecycle: manage_roles limited to project), infra_admin (manage deployments across tenants), security_admin (view/export audit, manage_policy), billing_admin (billing_*), super_admin (full - restricted to breakglass with approvals). Each template maps to permission primitives with an explicit allowed scope set.
permission_matrix:
Role	Global	Organization	Tenant	Project	Resource
viewer	read:list	read:list	read:list	read	read
developer	-	-	create:model,deploy	create,deploy,write	invoke:read
operator	-	manage:deployments	scale,deploy	deploy,scale,observe	invoke:manage
manager	-	manage:projects	manage:roles,manage:policies	manage:all	manage:resource
security_admin	view_audit,export_audit	view_audit	view_audit	view_audit	view_audit
infra_admin	manage_infra	manage_infra	manage_infra	-	-
billing_admin	billing_read,billing_write	billing_read	billing_read	-	-
super_admin	ALL	ALL	ALL	ALL	ALL
conflict_resolution: Evaluation precedence: explicit deny > explicit allow at same scope > allow from higher scope > conditional allows (require approval metadata). If multiple bindings grant different permission levels, the engine chooses the least-privileged effective permission unless an explicit allow escalates via approved elevation.
migration_strategy: Phased migration: 1) Read-only compatibility layer that maps v1 role names to RoleSet templates (feature flag). 2) Allow customers to preview effective permissions in console (simulation mode) for 2 weeks. 3) Write-path migration: create RoleSets for tenant admins and export existing bindings into RoleSet bindings with retained 'created_by' metadata. 4) Offer a one-click migration for simple tenants; complex tenants receive a guided migration plan. Data migration steps recorded in migration table with idempotent up/down scripts and backfill of audit entries.
audit_integration: All grant/revoke/elevation operations emit structured audit events: event_type, actor_id, principal, binding_id, role_template, scope, resource_urn, timestamp, ip, request_id, pre_state_digest, post_state_digest, approval_reference (if any), and sarif-like reason field. Audit events must be exported to: internal event pipeline, tenant audit log (retention policy), and optional external syslog/SEIM. Ensure logs are tamper-evident: events are signed with KMS key and include append-only sequence numbers per-tenant.
sso_mapping: SAML/OIDC mapping patterns: 1) Attribute-based mapping: map SAML attribute 'roles' or 'groups' to RoleSet names. 2) Rules engine: allow mapping rules like 'if group matches /^redwood-admins/ then bind super_admin@organization with expiration 1h for breakglass'. 3) SCIM: maintain group->RoleSet bindings and reconcile on sync. 4) Recommended practice: prefer group-to-roleset mappings and avoid individual direct grants created by SSO sync to reduce lifecycle churn.
admin_controls: Delegation: allow scoped 'role_grant' permission to be delegated with a max TTL and require justification. Emergency breakglass: support time-limited super_admin tokens that require approval audit and centralized revocation. Approval workflows: create approval_request objects tied to binding changes; approval can be synchronous (UI modal) or asynchronous (email/Slack). Rate-limits and guardrails: limit number of role grants per principal per hour and require multi-approver for cross-tenant elevation.
access_review: Implement automated quarterly recertification jobs that generate suggested revocations for stale grants (last used > 90 days and not granted as delegated). Provide audit dashboard for tenant admins and platform security to run ad-hoc access reviews. Include 'last_used' metadata on bindings derived from token usage logs.
rollout_plan: 1) Design review and sketches (this ticket). 2) RFC and API schema (ENG-90300). 3) Policy engine MVP behind feature flag in platform staging. 4) Canary rollout to internal Redwood tenants and 3 pilot customers. 5) Gradual ramp with telemetry: #failed_authorizations, average policy eval latency, migration opt-in rate. 6) Full rollout after 6 weeks of stable canary and security review sign-off.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Definitive role templates and permission primitives documented. 2) Deterministic inheritance semantics with unit tests covering edge cases. 3) Audit events emitted for all binding changes and elevation flows with required fields present. 4) SSO mapping patterns validated with a test SAML IdP and SCIM sync integration tests. 5) Migration tooling can perform a dry-run and produce a migration plan summary for a tenant. 6) Performance: policy evaluation latency P95 < 3ms under typical load (10k QPS simulated).
open_questions: 1) Should wildcard scope grants (e.g., project:*) be allowed or strictly avoided? 2) Precedence with external policies (cloud IAM) - how to model conflicting denies? 3) How to surface 'approved' vs 'auto' elevations in console UI to minimize confusion? 4) Is 'impersonate' allowed for infra_admin by default or require explicit opt-in? 5) Retention policy defaults for tenant audit exports.
